text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Electoral commission set to check fraud as registration of voters for transition to civil rule begins on Monday.

- Central bank shortlists 57 banks to take over its retail functions as specified in the 1997 fiscal budget under which ministries and official agencies now have to keep their money in commercial banks.
- Nigeria conquers Europe, beat Spain 3-2 in under-17 maiden Africa/Europe Soccer championship in Portugal.
- Federal government approves 40 percent rise in domestic air fares.
- A desperate manoeuvre to avoid collision with another airliner is believed to have caused last November's crash of ADC airline's plane which killed all 143 on board, sources say.
- Nigerian government initiates diplomatic moves to resolve crisis over withdrawal of Italy from buying liquefied natural gas that Nigeria is to bring on stream in 1999.
- About 36 oil firms will from Tuesday present their plan of activities to the Department of Petroleum Resources, the industry regulator, for screening as required annually.
- British Telecom severs all links with Nigerian Telecommunications Ltd following cancellation of a $225 million Work Bank telecoms improvement loan, sources say.
- Vehicle imports to Nigeria decline by 60 percent to 33,210 last year from 87,000 at the peak of import of cars in 1991, according to port figures.

- Former presidential aspirants Olu Falae and Frederick Fasehun, who are being detained over bomb blasts in Lagos may be tried under a new decree to curb political violence and boost the transition to democracy programme, sources say.
- Federal government pays $1 million debt owed Aer Lingus of Ireland by troubled national carrier Nigeria Airways.
